item.title: Strong M6.2 earthquake hits Coquimbo Region, Chile
item.description: A strong earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.2 struck the Coquimbo Region, Chile, at 13:34 UTC (10:34 local time) on February 12, 2026. The agency is reporting a depth of 37 km (22.9 miles). EMSC is reporting the same magnitude and depth. Source

item.title: Gezani forecast to reach intense tropical cyclone strength near Mozambique coast, more than 1 million at risk
item.description: Tropical Cyclone Gezani was located in the Mozambique Channel at 12:00 UTC on February 12, 2026, with maximum sustained winds of 120 km/h (75 mph) and is forecast to intensify to 165 km/h (105 mph) near the Mozambique coast by February 14. item.title: Bright fireball recorded over Indiana–Ohio border region
item.description: A bright fireball was observed over the Indiana–Ohio border region at 04:31 UTC on February 11, 2026 (23:32 local time on February 10), generating more than 120 eyewitness reports across five U.S. states. The meteor was first detected at an altitude of 76 km (47 miles) near Trinity, Indiana, and disintegrated at 43 km (27 miles) above Laura, Ohio. The object traveled approximately 77 km (48 miles) through the atmosphere at a speed of 13 km/s (29 000 mph). Source

item.title: Maryland reports at least 15 cold-related deaths after January 2026 snowstorm
item.description: At least 15 cold-related deaths were reported in Maryland in the two weeks after a historic winter storm affected the United States in late January 2026. Source

item.title: At least 11 dead as avalanches strike multiple Alpine sites in Italy and France
item.description: Snow avalanches struck northern Italy and south-eastern France between February 7--8, 2026, killing at least 11 people across multiple Alpine locations. Italian authorities reported several fatalities in Trentino–Alto Adige and Lombardy, while French media confirmed deaths in the Hautes-Alpes. The incidents occurred during a period of elevated avalanche danger following recent snowfall and wind loading. Source

item.title: Storm Nils kills 1 in France, triggers rare Red Avalanche Alert in Savoie as 850 000 lose power
item.description: At least one person was reported dead as Storm Nils brought damaging winds to France late on February 11, 2026, with gusts exceeding 180 km/h (112 mph) recorded in parts of the country. More than 900 000 customers were left without power as authorities issued red and orange alerts across multiple departments, while Savoie was placed under a rare red avalanche alert on February 12 after multiple avalanches were reported. Source

item.title: Pair of mid-level troughs forecast to bring widespread precipitation to California
item.description: Two mid-level troughs with associated surface lows are forecast to bring widespread precipitation to California between February 14 and 19, 2025. The first system is forecast to begin affecting the state on February 14–15, followed by a second trough deepening offshore from February 16–17. Snowfall totals over the Sierra Nevada could exceed 60 cm (24 inches), while rainfall totals of 25–50 mm (1–2 inches) are forecast across much of the state during the initial 72-hour period. Source

item.title: Gezani destroys 18 800 homes, claims 40 lives in Madagascar
item.description: At least 40 fatalities have been confirmed, and over 18 800 homes have been destroyed as of February 13, 2026, since Tropical Cyclone Gezani made landfall over Madagascar. The storm remains active and is forecast to continue intensifying through February 13 while remaining in open waters. Source

item.title: Florida enters worst drought in 25 years as extreme conditions expand
item.description: Florida has entered its worst drought in 25 years, with 100.00% of the state classified in drought categories D0--D4, according to the U.S. Drought Monitor. Severe to extreme drought now covers 85.46% of the state, marking the most extensive spatial coverage since the 2000--2001 drought event. Source

item.title: Strong and shallow M6.4 earthquake hits near Port-Olry, Vanuatu
item.description: A strong and shallow earthquake registered by the USGS as M6.4 struck near Port-Olry, Vanuatu at 02:27 UTC on February 14, 2026. The agency is reporting a depth of 10 km (6.2 miles). The EMSC is reporting M6.5 at the same depth. According to the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center (PTWC), there is no tsunami threat from this earthquake. Source
